report.summary: 5 findings: 2 high, 3 medium. Top priority: fix REPORT_SCHEMA to allow structured handoff; verify containment guarantees; check spectral truncation; audit ledger.close() and live_egress_seats.
risks: Handoff data loss: downstream modules may silently lose structured data.
Containment guarantee unverified: missing functions could allow write escape.
Spectral truncation mismatch: potential index errors in downstream consumers.
Silent exception swallowing: may mask corruption or resource leaks.
Live_egress_reuse: duplication could lead to inconsistency in provider health checks.
todos: Inspect daedalus/eval/report.py and modify REPORT_SCHEMA to allow structured handoff (e.g., additional fields or a handoff object).
Search daedalus/spine/attempt.py and daedalus/spine/containment.py for 'Job Object', 'refusal_attestation', '_remove_gate_tmpdir'. If missing, define them or update docstring.
Search for consumers of topology.eigenvalues in daedalus/structcore/ and adjust truncation or downstream code to handle mismatched lengths.
Inspect close() in daedalus/spine/ledger.py and add logging or re-raise exceptions appropriately.
Inspect live_egress_seats in daedalus/council/session.py and refactor to delegate to available_providers or provider_health.
Write tests for each fix to verify correctness.

items.title: Fix REPORT_SCHEMA to allow structured handoff data
items.why_now: The strict schema strips structured data, breaking downstream consumers that expect more than a notes string. This is a high-severity data loss bug.

steps.do: Open daedalus/eval/report.py and modify REPORT_SCHEMA to allow an optional 'handoff' object with additional fields (e.g., churn results). Set additionalProperties to true or define explicit properties.
steps.verified_by: Run existing tests for report schema and handoff; verify that structured data passes through.

items.assumption: REPORT_SCHEMA is defined in daedalus/eval/report.py and is the only place that restricts handoff.

items.title: Verify and fix containment guarantees in attempt.py and containment.py
items.why_now: The docstring claims guarantees that depend on missing functions. If those functions are absent, the containment is unenforced, allowing write escape.

steps.do: Search daedalus/spine/attempt.py and daedalus/spine/containment.py for 'Job Object', 'refusal_attestation', '_remove_gate_tmpdir'. If any are missing, define them or update the docstring to reflect actual guarantees.
steps.verified_by: grep -n 'Job Object\|refusal_attestation\|_remove_gate_tmpdir' daedalus/spine/attempt.py daedalus/spine/containment.py; ensure all three exist.

items.assumption: The functions are not defined elsewhere (e.g., in other files not cited).

items.title: Fix spectral truncation mismatch in topology.py
items.why_now: Truncating eigenvalues to 8 when component_count > 8 can cause index errors in downstream consumers that expect len(eigenvalues) == component_count.

steps.do: Search for code that consumes topology.eigenvalues (e.g., in daedalus/structcore/ or daedalus/mapping/). Check if any code uses len(eigenvalues) or iterates assuming one per component. If so, adjust truncation or downstream logic.
steps.verified_by: Write a test that creates a topology with component_count > 8 and verifies that downstream consumers handle the truncated list correctly.

items.assumption: Downstream consumers exist that rely on the exact count.

items.title: Audit ledger.close() exception swallowing in ledger.py
items.why_now: The close() method catches all sqlite3.Error and does nothing, potentially masking corruption or resource leaks.

steps.do: Inspect close() method in daedalus/spine/ledger.py. Add logging of the exception or re-raise if appropriate.
steps.verified_by: Run tests that trigger close() with a broken connection and verify that the exception is logged (or re-raised).

items.assumption: close() is defined in daedalus/spine/ledger.py and currently swallows exceptions.

items.title: Refactor live_egress_seats to delegate to available_providers
items.why_now: If live_egress_seats duplicates logic, it may become inconsistent with available_providers. Refactoring ensures a single source of truth for provider health.

steps.do: Inspect live_egress_seats in daedalus/council/session.py. If it does not delegate to available_providers or provider_health, refactor it to do so.
steps.verified_by: Run tests for session.py and verify that live_egress_seats returns the same results as available_providers.

items.assumption: live_egress_seats is defined in daedalus/council/session.py and currently duplicates logic.
